Use soft watercolor and gouache-like textures, gentle expressive linework, dimensional shading, warm whimsical charm, natural but adorable anatomy, rich yet tasteful color, and a premium hand-illustrated editorial finish. The subject should feel like it belongs in a professionally published children’s storybook for ages 3–8. The illustration must be expressive, polished, cute, and visually rich, with a transparent background and a clean standalone composition.
Art direction refinement: MUCH LESS REALISTIC, a loose painterly contemporary children's picture book. Broad visible gouache brush strokes, soft washes, playfully exaggerated chubby proportions, sweet small simple ink eyes, rounded organic asymmetry, restrained detail, tactile drybrush texture. Two or three soft painted color values suggest volume. No glossy big eyes, no anatomical microdetail, no individual realistic feathers or scales, no 3D rendering, no photographic lighting. It must still be a rich hand-painted illustration, never flat vector icon or emoji.
Use the attached bird ONLY as the style reference: match its loose brushwork, charming simplicity, soft shading and detail level. Generate a DIFFERENT subject: One small cohesive forest-clearing vignette, two whimsical sage-green trees framing a gently winding ochre footpath, little painted ferns and three red mushrooms. Loose brushstrokes and simplified foliage, no individual leaf detail. Organic irregular edge of this landscape with transparency all around, no rectangular sky, no animals.
ONE full isolated subject, centered, 12% clear margin, actual transparent background, no external haze, outline, text or border. Do not include the reference bird.
